articleTitle: The performance of backward curved centrifugal fan with various impeller inlet and outlet angles
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The backward curved centrifugal fan is the main component in air duct flow system. The fans consume approximately 15% of building energy consumption, therefore their efficiency critically impacts the energy demand and cost. The performance of a fan is determined by a number of design factors. In this study, the effect of the impeller's inlet and outlet angles on the fan performance was investigated using the CFD flow simulation. An experimental data was also collected from a model fan following the ISO 5801 standard for comparisons. Based on simulation results, an increase in the outlet angle from 30° to 40° at a constant inlet angle led to a higher air power (approximately 11%), whereas an increase in the inlet angle from 15° to 21° at a constant outlet angle causes minimal change to the air power (less that 0.4%). As the air power is related to the fan efficiency, the results have an implication on the design and manufacturing of a fan to ultimately lower the energy requirements in buildings.

articleTitle: Artificial Human Arm Controlled by Muscle Electromyography (EMG)
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: Disabled people with disabilities upper arms, elbows are more difficult to behave everyday life. The normal artificial arm cannot be used to hold the device easily. Development of a robotic arm can help to hold the prosthetic hand. It will help the disabled people to stay more comfortable. The main structure of the mechanical arm is made by using lightweight aluminum. Moving fingers using servo motors and push-pull fingers by sling. However, sensor which is communicate with human being is the main issue. Using sensor pad or mechanical movement sensor are impossible to assembly to people who disabilities at upper arms. Research presents sensor system using EMG sensor. EMG uses principle of electromyography by measure electrical signal which generate directly from muscle. To control the servo motor. Artificial arm is design by human physiology. 3D printer is printed to create the real artificial arm and finger. Using this system is quite difficult to control because user do not have the experience to control the energy from muscle. The user has to train the movement of the back muscles.

articleTitle: Life-Time-Assessment for Rotors for Electric Drives
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The rotors of electric motors for vehicle drives are subject to time-varying loads in customer use due to mechanical, magnetic, electrical and thermal forces. To ensure the operational safety of the electric motor throughout the design life, a computational or experimental life-time assessment has to be performed. For this purpose, both the loading of the rotor as well as the resistance of the electric strip must be known. In this paper the loading situation of the rotor blades under service conditions is estimated with a simplified model which takes mechanical and magnetic forces into account. For the theoretical life-time-assessment the relevant material parameter under fatigue loading of the thin electrical steel must be known. While there are established and proven procedures both for proof of fatigue strength and for determining the required characteristic values for steel sheets for use in the bodywork and chassis area, there is still no corresponding procedure for the very thin electrical steel bands. The paper shows possibilities for the experimental determination of the fatigue strength characteristics. In addition, influencing factors on the fatigue behavior of electrical steel are shown.

articleTitle: Using MATLAB V&V-Toolbox for Target-Specific Model-Based Design
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: A major advantage of Model-Based Design is the thorough verification of algorithms within a simulation. The same results are far more difficult to achieve via classical code testing approaches. However, when considering a target specific model for series code production, certain restrictions arise regarding the model architecture when employing the V&V toolchain. This paper discusses an approach overcoming these restrictions, resulting in a complete verification of the software specifications.

articleTitle: Contactless Distance Sensor for small air-gap (<10 mm) using Linear Hall Effect Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: This paper presents a contactless method to measure small air-gap distance (<;10 mm) using linear Hall effect sensor. The method exploited measurement of changes in magnetic field intensity as a function of Hall sensor displacement. The results showed that the displacements were exponentially correlated with output signal from Hall sensor. The empirical equation of the displacement as a function of the output signal was generated using the exponential regression agreement analysis. The statistical analysis of the predicted displacement in comparison to the actual displacement indicated strong correlation coefficient R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.9932 and low absolute percentage mean error of 4.6784%. In addition, a potential application of surface crack detection on ferromagnetic materials is also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Application of AERMOD Model with Clean Technology Principles for Industrial Air Pollution Reduction
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: This paper presents a case study of air pollution reduction analysis for a medium-sized starch factory in Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand. Pertinent data surveyed and gathered included the factory basic information, production processes, air pollutant emission inventory, and air pollution measurements. The U.S.EPA's AERMOD air quality model was used to estimate current pollutant levels at nearby receptors and possible pollutant reduction resulting from suggested clean technology options. The analysis yielded 3 groups of 12 options. They were: (1) improvement at the tapioca stockpile area, (2) improvement at the starch drying process, and (3) improvement of the hot-air generators. The estimation by AERMOD showed the 12 options can reduce ambient dust and SO2 concentration levels at the receptors up to 44% and 30%, respectively. Evaluation results indicated that installment of a bag filter system and heat-recovery economizers for all 3 hot-air generators were the factory's most appropriate options - with respect to technical, economical, and environmental evaluation - for reducing the air pollution impacts to its community.

articleTitle: Frequency Response System Identification and Flight Controller Tuning for Quadcopter UAV
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: This paper presents methodology to determine dynamic models and the suitable controllers for FY450 Firefly quadcopter. Frequency response system identification technique via software package Comprehensive Identification from Frequency Response (CIFER) was applied in this research. Pixhawk hardware with PX4 Flight stack firmware was implemented as a flight controller. The measurement of inputs and outputs during hovering flight maneuver with frequency sweep input was utilized to determine the unknown parameters of SISO mathematical model. Then after mathematical models were identified, the dynamic models of roll, pitch and yaw response respectively were employed to tuning the gains of PX4 controller structure with globally offline optimization technique. With this presented method, satisfied flight dynamics meets the desired performances without the requirement of numerous in-flight tuning.

articleTitle: Effect of Heat treatment on Single Point Incremental Forming for Titanium Grade 2 Sheet
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: This research aims to investigate the effect of heat treatment for the incremental forming process of titanium grade 2 sheet. The specimen profile was designed by Unigraphics NX4 and formed on CNC machining center to a 25 mm radius dome-like profile, using molybdenum disulfide as a lubricant. By applying a step depth at 1 mm, there was no tearing of the titanium sheet at the profile depth of 11 mm. From this stage, this pre-formed titanium sheet was heated in an oven at 580°C and 750°C as a stress relieving and annealing temperature respectively. Afterward, the forming experiments were further conducted with designated temperature in order to study its formability, in which oxy-acetylene torch was used as an elevated temperature source using a computer controller via the control box at temperatures range between 300°C to 800°C. It was found that heat treatment during forming process was capable to manufacture a dome-like profile at a maximum depth of 25 mm, which was more than a merely stress relieving and annealing temperature which had maximum depth at 12 mm). Therefore, a combination of heat treatment methods can be usefully applied to a deep shape forming of a titanium sheet by SPIF process.

articleTitle: Experimental study on compressive behavior of low and normal strength concrete confined by low-cost glass fiber reinforced polymers (GFRP)
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The main objective of this study is to investigate the performance of low-cost glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) in strengthening normal (15MPa) and low strength (5MPa) concrete cylinders. Typically, the strengthening technique using FRP is often expensive and may not be economically used for reinforced concrete (RC) houses in rural area. In many cases, the concrete strength used for these house constructions is often low. Therefore, the capability of low-cost GFRP in strengthening low strength concrete compared with normal strength concrete has been investigated. A total of 8 cylindrical specimens with the dimensions of 150 mm x 300 mm (diameter x height) were tested under compressive loading. Half of these specimens possess compressive strength of 5 MPa and the rest have 15 MPa compressive strength. The specimens were unconfined and also confined with GFRP one, two and three layers. It was found that, for 5 MPa compressive strength cylinder, the compressive strength of the specimens has increase 2.27 MPa, 3.96 MPa and 4.31 MPa for one, two and three-layer GFRP wrapping respectively compared to the controlled specimen. For 15 MPa compressive strength cylinder, the compressive strength of the specimens has increase 1.75 MPa, 2.29 MPa and 2.95 MPa for one, two and three-layer GFRP wrapping respectively compared to the controlled specimen. The test result showed that the use of low-cost GFRP is one of the effective and economical method to improve compressive strength of low strength concrete.

articleTitle: An Automatic Stabilizing System for Balancing a Multi-Rotor Subject to Variations in Center of Gravity and Mass
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The objectives of this study are to design and construct a multi-rotor helicopter along with the automatic stabilizing system due to center of gravity moving forward to in front of its frame. Nowadays a multi-rotor helicopter is popularly using on account of lightweight and high lift force. However, it is utilized to carry a payload or install some device that affect to center of gravity moving during flight that it may lead to be unstable in control. In this paper, the quad-rotor helicopter has been designed and constructed with automatic stabilizing system. The stabilizing system depends on automatic movement of mass of some aircraft component installed to counterbalance when center of gravity is changed. An unbalanced signal between observe motor inputs in front and rear side are assigned to be input command for feedback control of stabilizing system in order to counterbalance in the suitable center of gravity. The mentioned stabilizing system is implemented with Firefly 450 quad-rotor frame. A result illustrates that the additionally automatic stabilizing system of quad-rotor helicopter aids to control effectively and stable.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation for Soil Surface Explosion Problem - A study of fragments controlling effect using liner plate application –
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The main objective of our research is to contribute to a technique of unexploded bomb (UXB) disposal such as an establishment of evacuation areas based on the computational mechanics. To reveal the fragments behavior such as shells, explosives and soils, the computational model based on the SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) schemes have been constructed with HyperWorks-RADIOSS (®Altair) software. In this report, we addressed the effects of the difference amounts of shells and explosives on the fragments behavior. And then, the computational models including a liner plate, which are corrugated thin steel sheet, have been developed. By conducting a series of numerical simulation, we investigated the protection capability of fragments about the liner plate and we also discussed the reduction of an evacuation areas.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on the Behavior of a Common Rail Diesel-Engine Fueled with Diesel Dimethyl Ether Dual Fuel on Engine Performance
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: Dimethyl ether (DME) - diesel dual fuel combustion has shown the potential in reducing nitrogen monoxide and improving the engine performance compared to diesel operation. This study is an investigation of dual fuel with diesel and DME Port Fuel Injection (PFI) on pilot fuel injection using a common rail diesel engine. The main injection timing was at 20 degrees of crank angle before top dead center. In addition, the pilot fuel injector timing before the main injection was 10 degrees of crank angle, with only 0.5 milliseconds of time. The common rail engine is operated with 0 - 70% DME compared with main fuel. The main finding shows that the combustion of 10%DME emitted low nitrogen monoxide content and enhanced thermal efficiency compared with only pilot fuel injection. However, the higher ratio of DME port fuel injection is affected to the increasing of nitrogen monoxide, carbon monoxide and hydrocarbon content. In additions, DME port injection of 50% reduced the diesel fuel consumption up to 32.17 %.

articleTitle: A Systematic Approach to Design Automatic Workpiece Changer of CNC Machining Center
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The automatic machine running industrial production line, with 3 main processes both loading and unloading processes in consecutive, faces a difficulty in working processes between machine and operators. Since the whole process is conducted by workers and require several procedures, this leads to the delay and inefficiency of the production line. The number of workers is demanded in direct variation with production intensity, leading to higher cost. In order to increase efficiency of the machine and reduce procedure of workers, this research aims to propose an Automatic Workpiece Changer System (AWCs) to work in current with CNC Machining Center. The study and analysis of tasks throughout the process, bring about the design specification to apply in a systematic approach in engineering design. The black-box diagram is used in the analysis of functions and sub-functions of the system, and also their interconnection, which will be transformed to the design specification. Then the alternative design concepts are generated and illustrated in the morphological chart, in which the most suitable concept will be selected and used to create the prototype. In conclusion, the AWCs consist of 5 modules; Tray in, Gripper, Tightening, Fixture, and Tray out, 6 tasks of workers are transferred to the machine.

articleTitle: Impact of Compressed Biogas on Combustion and Exhaust Emission Characteristic from Spark Ignition Engine
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The demand of fossil fuel for transportation increases continuously while the fossil fuels resource is limit. Hence, the aim of experimental study is to investigate the effect of compress biogas as the alternative fuels on engine performance and emission in modified SI engine. The engine was modified and replaced fuel metering system to compress biogas system with standard ignition system configuration. The gas engine was operated under various engine speed (1500 - 3000 rpm) and different engine load at 25%, 50% and 75% of maximum load. The result shows that the gas engine fuelled with compressed biogas can enhance engine performance with low exhaust gas emission. Therefore, the utilization of compressed biogas is highly potential for automobile since it reduces the reliance on fossil fuels. In addition, compression biogas can support the growing demand of transportation fuels in the future.

articleTitle: Simulation of Stenosis in Blood Vessel by Lattice Boltzmann Method
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) for blood flow has been applied, the lattice Boltzmann model used in two dimensions and nine directions (D2Q9), solving by the Navier-Stokes (NS) equation with the Lattice Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (LBGK) method and the equation of continuity with the Poiseuille's law to describe the behavior of the blood flow. In this work a LBM is used to simulate blood flow in case of stenosis in blood vessel and observe blood flow in condition of Raynolds number changes in blood vessel. The simulation results will show the velocity of blood flow and the high pressures emerge stenosis in blood vessel during to the obstacle become bigger in blood vessel with the time step in simulation.

articleTitle: A study of fuel spray simulations under non-reacting condition in a constant volume chamber by LES
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: For engine analysis, an accurately capturing physics of fuel injection, spray breakup and spray vaporization are needed. To obtain the jet spray characteristics in more detail, the spray bomb simulations are a better method to isolate the spray patterns. In the research, the experiments of spray bomb with a constant volume chamber without the moving boundaries are chosen to be a test case. The commercial code ANSYS Forte is used to simulate fuel sprays and Large Eddy Simulation techniques (LES) with a dynamic structure model are employed to capture flow fields and internal spray structures. The simulated spray results are validated with available experimental data from Sandia National Laboratories USA using n-heptane fuel under non-reacting conditions. The predicted results of liquid and vapor penetration length are presented by LES simulations. The simulated vapor penetration is over-predicted in the early stage and matched well with experimental data after t = 0.75 ms. The increase of ambient pressure has made the decrease of the vapor and liquid penetration length. The transient behaviors of temperature and velocity are also captured in this study.

articleTitle: Investigation of Control Variable Effects on Combustion Parameters under Lean Operation Mode
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of control variables, which are throttle angle (TA), spark advance (SA) and variable valve timing (VVT), on combustion parameters of a commercial gasoline engine under lean combustion. The parameters considered in this work are the location of 50% of mass fraction burned (CA50) and the location of peak pressure (LPP). These parameters are calculated online using the algorithm that can be implemented on MATLAB/Simulink platform and then complied in C-code and real-time executed on the dSPACE1006. The lean combustion experiments are conducted on the engine test bench consists of a six cylinders gasoline commercial engine with a low inertia dynamometer. Based on the experimental results, the effects of considered control variables on combustion parameters can be investigated. Additionally, we can use this information for improvement of lean combustion control performance and reduce the combustion variability.

articleTitle: Experimental Comparison of TIG and Friction Stir Welded for Dissimilar Aluminum Alloy Plates
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: In this investigation, an attempt has been made to study the experimental comparison of the macrostructural and mechanical characteristics of fusion welds (TIG) and solid-state welds (FSW) of dissimilar aluminum alloy plates, SSM356 and SSM6061 (as-cast and T6). Aluminum alloys of 4 mm thickness were used as the base material for preparing a butt joint welded. The preliminary results of aluminum alloys in the as-cast condition showed that TIG (with filler), TIG (without filler) and friction stir welding made good welded joints of dissimilar aluminum alloys. The result of aluminum alloys in the heat treatment (T6) condition showed that different welding process could make dissimilar aluminum alloy joints. The ultimate tensile strength of dissimilar joints by FSW was 168.32 MPa and was superior to TIG (with filler) and TIG (without filler) welding. The study found that the two welding parameters significantly affect the tensile strength of the weld at the 0.05 level of significance. The experimental values were in good agreement with an R2 of 92.45 for ultimate tensile strength.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design Considerations of Wideband Radome for Antenna Array of Digital Television Broadcasting Transmission
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The electromagnetic properties are considered for the radome design of the wideband application in digital television (DTV) antenna array used for broadcasting transmission. The manufactured material with associated geometry is appropriately chosen to achieve the optimum radiation performances. The radome design guidelines for the wideband DTV antenna array of the broadcasting transmission are provided. The presented information is significant for DTV antenna array of future development.

articleTitle: Effect of process parameter and gate size on gate freeze time in injection molding by using simulation software
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: Gate freeze time is played important role in injection molding cycle time. It indicates that when should be the end of the packing time that affect part quality. If packing phase not hold until the gate freeze. The part weight tends to light and may be sink. This work has studied the effect of melt temperature, mold temperature and gate size on gate freeze time. Two type of polymer were used acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) and polypropylene (PP). The Moldex3D program was used to find out the gate freeze time. The loop cooling channel used on both side of molding. The injection parameter such as stroke time, setting injection pressure, packing time and packing pressure are the same setting for all experiment. The result showed that the huge different gate freeze time with the different material. Similarly, gate thickness was effect to gate solidification time. The temperature also affects to gate freeze time especially melt temperature, whereas gate wideness and mold temperature had no significant effect on gate freeze time. This experiment could help the designer to understand about these factors was effect to gate freeze time.

articleTitle: Combustion Characteristics of Diesohol Fuel in a Modern Diesel Engine
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: To reduce diesel consumption, alternative fuels such as biodiesel have been studies to use in compression ignition (CI) engines. However, biodiesel is still limited to a maximum concentration of 7 % in Thailand. Therefore, other alternative fuels have been searched to replace diesel use. Due to its oversupply in domestic market, ethanol is one of the promising fuel to apply in the CI engine. To use as the blend called diesohol, ethanol is mixed with diesel which added biodiesel as an additive to prevent phase separation. This study has investigated the use to diesohol in a modern diesel engine. Engine performance, fuel consumption and exhaust emissions including HC, NOX were measured. Also, formaldehyde and acetaldehyde formed during ethanol combustion were evaluated. To clearly understand the effect of ethanol on the engine performance and emissions, combustion characteristics was studies by means of in-cylinder pressure measurement. The percentage of ethanol, mixed in the blend, was varied as 5 and 10 %v/v while the concentration of biodiesel was added as 3, 7 and 10 % v/v. The result shows that engine torque and power were reduced when using diesohol as the fuel. HC and NOX were increased as well as carbonyl emissions were higher than the engine using diesel fuel.

articleTitle: A Shelling Machine for Inca Peanuts
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: Inca peanut is a new economic crop with increasing popularity across Thailand, both for plantation and processing. It is also in high demand in the AEC and global markets. Shelling is an important step in the preparation of the seeds processing. However, due to the limitation of the shapes and the fact that the seeds have three layers, the shelling process is often a major impediment of the production process. Therefore, this research aims at designing and constructing a shelling machine for Inca peanuts, which are brown seeds. The study comprises 3 parts: a study of the physical properties, the design and construction, and a performance test for the shelling machine. The shelling machine was made up of 2 primary parts, which were the rotary feeder and the shelling set. The rotary feeder had a diameter of 100 mm. with a length of 120 mm. and had 4 fin-like components. The shelling set had a diameter of 320 mm. with a ball length of 430 mm. There were 4 straps placed at a 90-degree angle adjacent to the radius. The test revealed that the shelling works at a shaft speed of 270 rpm. The clearance of 20 mm. with the outlet of 2.0×8.0 cm. This was an appropriate condition for shelling with an average shelling efficiency percentage of 81.59 %. Percentage of Whole nut at 62.23 %; Percentage of broken nut at 3.26 %; Percentage of broken kernel at 4.74 %, and Percentage of unshelled seeds at 29.77 %. The working capacity was 70.22 kg/hr.

articleTitle: Impact of PWM Modulation Schemes on Common-Mode Voltage Generated by 3-Level Neutral-Point-Clamped Inverters
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study on the impacts of various carrier-based PWM modulation schemes in terms of common-mode voltages generated by 3-level neutral-point-clamped inverters. In these modulation techniques, various third harmonic voltage are injected into reference sinusoidal voltages to improve modulation index, switching losses and harmonics quality. The simulation results of the common-mode voltage waveforms and their spectrums show that injected zero sequence voltages can directly affect the generated common-mode voltages, not only in the range of harmonic frequencies, which are the frequencies of the zero sequence signal, but also in the high-frequency range, which can potentially cause EMI problems.

articleTitle: Design Concept of Low Cost Measurement for Motor Current Signature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: This paper presents a concept of low cost current measurement for motor current signature analysis (MCSA). The motor current is measured and then its spectrum is analyzed to estimate the faults. This method is widely accepted for fault diagnostic of induction motors. Since the frequency spectrum of motor current is characterized by different types of faults, the sampling frequency must be high enough to get adequate information from motor current for all cases of fault. In addition to sampling frequency, the measuring time must be long enough to collect data to differentiate the fundamental frequency and interharmonics which are relatively closed to each other. Therefore, using high sampling frequencies results in a large memory required for storing measured data and a powerful processor to handle the large amount of data. It leads to increase the cost of measurement The design concept is proposed an optimal sampling frequency and measuring time for the measurement by using multi sampling frequencies suitable for the frequency spectrum of each faults. In this paper, there are two sampling rates, a low sampling rate to handle low frequency spectrum and the other for high frequency spectrum. Spectrum analysis is performed to the sampled current signals by fast Fourier transform (FFT) and Welch's technique. The comparison between the high sampling frequencies and the proposed frequency presents the performance of the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Study on Relationship of the Material Removal Amount and the Increase in Abrasive Nanoparticle Size during Si-CMP
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) of silicon wafer is indispensable for providing the substrate used in manufacturing of semiconductor device. However, the CMP process has many parameters, such as polishing pressure, platen/carrier rotational speed, polishing pad characteristics, chemical solution/abrasive in polishing slurry. In these parameters, abrasive particles in the slurry have both mechanical and chemical actions. To enhance the CMP process efficiency, we have been studied the relationship between the Material Removal Amount (MRA) and the increase of abrasive particle size during CMP. In this report, the colloidal silica abrasive nanoparticle sizes of 20 nm and 55 nm were used for polishing the Silicon wafers by a CMP machine, which is installed a slurry pool. A dynamic light scattering (DLS) spectra measures the increase in abrasive nanoparticle sizes. The silicon particle size after CMP process were direct proportion with MRA of Si-wafer was polished.

articleTitle: Influence of Nickel Powder on Microstructure of Carbon Steel Weld using GMAW
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The purpose of this research was studied overlay weld of ASTM A36 carbon steel using gas metal arc welding (GMAW) without and with nickel powder adding. ER 70S-6 filler metal consumable electrode was used in diameter 2 mm. Metallurgical structure was examined using an optical microscope (OM). In addition, the mechanical property of the weldment evaluated by micro vickers hardness was measured by means of the variation in the percentage of nickel powder adding. The weldment without and with adding nickel powder 4.25, 7.25 and 15.75 g/min were produced and carried out to the metallography analysis, The experimental result showed that defect-free of all welded-specimens. The highest value of microhardness was 527.4 Hv with the nickel powder 15.75 g/min. Moreover, the hardness of weld metal tends to decrease with decreasing of the weight fraction of nickel adding.

Author Keywords: microstructure and gas metal arc welding

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Threading Machine for Tobacco Leaves
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: Threading tobacco leaf is a step in the manufacturing of Thai tobacco cigars to ease the process of sun drying. At present, farmers are threading tobacco leaf manually, which results in a low output. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to design and develop a threading machine for a small group of farmers. The machine was divided into three units: a round tray conveyor, threading, and gathering units. A one- horsepower electric motor was used to drive the round tray conveyor that specified the strokes made by a Geneva mechanism. The threading and gathering units were driven by a pneumatic system while the opening/closing of valves, cylinders, and clippers were operated by a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC). For this study, there were three different tangential velocities of trays (0.131, 0.157 and 0.183 m/s) and two different numbers of threading per single gathering (seven and eight trays/gathering). The result showed a 0.157 m/s tangential velocity of trays, and threading with seven trays/gathering was the optimum, which obtained 4,570 leaves/hour (nine bunches/hour) per field capacity and 95.2% threading and gathering efficiency.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Performance of the Micro Direct Ethanol Fuel Cell
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The direct ethanol fuel cell (DEFC) is selected for this research. DEFC uses ethanol in the fuel cell instead of the more toxic methanol. Ethanol is more attractive than methanol by many reasons. Ethanol is a hydrogen-rich liquid and it has a higher specific energy (8.0 kWh/kg) compared to methanol (6.1 kWh/kg). Ethanol can be obtained in great quantity from biomass through a fermentation process from renewable resources like from sugar cane, wheat, corn, or even straw. The use of ethanol would also overcome both the storage and infrastructure challenge of hydrogen for fuel cell applications. The experimental apparatus on the micro direct ethanol fuel cell for measuring the cell performance has been set for this research. The goal of the DEFC study in this research was studied on the performance of the micro direct ethanol fuel cell (Micro-DEFC). The experimental performance testing were studied about three kinds of the ethanol blended. There are the ethanol was blended with pure distilled water, the ethanol was blended with conventional drinking water and the ethanol was blended with normal tap water. The effect of operating temperature change on the electrical production is also study too. The cell performance is specified in the terms of cell voltage and power of the cell. By observing for all three experiments, increasing the volume of ethanol and the cell operating temperature effect on the electrical production of the fuel cell. By increasing the volume of ethanol and the temperature, the fuel cell gradually produce the electrical value and gradually increase to the maximum value, and then gradually decrease until the fuel has been depleted. Increasing the volumetric of ethanol and cell operating temperature effect on the electrical current production and power of the fuel cell but do not affect on the electrical potential or have a little effect. Compared to the three experiments, the third experiment that the ethanol was blended with normal tap water. Due to the impurity of the water, the crossing of the water from the electrode to the electrode within the electrochemical reaction zone of the fuel cell results in the abrasion of the electrochemical reaction of the fuel cell. So, it is given the low fuel cell production capacity.

articleTitle: Advancing the State of the Art in Automotive Software Testing by Certification
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: Testing is the most important activity in quality assurance for software. To ensure that there are enough qualified testers to do the testing, and to make sure that these testers are well trained, the International Software Qualification Board (ISTQB®) introduced the Certified Tester Foundation Level (CTFL®) in 2002. The CTFL program aims at ensuring that all certified testers have a common understanding of software testing - independent of the product domain. So far, more than 500,000 testers worldwide passed the CTFL certification.However, each product domain has specific characteristics and constraints that must be considered when qualifying testers for that domain. This applies especially to the automotive domain, which has international and national regulations, standards, and technologies. These have a high impact on automotive software testing. Additionally, with the introduction of electric, connected and autonomous vehicles, the amount of software in the car is rising significantly. The ISTQB is introducing an add-on qualification to the CTFL for the automotive domain: the CTFL Specialist Automotive Software Tester (CTFL-AuT). The CTFL-AuT gives testers with a CTFL all the necessary background and additional skills for the automotive domain. This paper describes the objectives, the content, and first experiences with the CTFL-AuT qualification program.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Hydrogen Production from Compression Ignition Engine Fueled with Biodiesel-Diesel Fuel Blends via Reforming Process
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: This paper aim to find feasibility of hydrogen production via biodiesel fuel exhaust gas reforming. The examined process base on platinum-rhodium alumina catalyst, intend application for compression ignition engine, fuel cells and after-treatment technologies. This research are investigated the exhaust gas composition (e.g. O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) under different engine conditions under no modification engine. The comparison between biodiesel 50%Vol. blends with diesel 50%Vol. (DB50) fuel and pure biodiesel (B100) on combustion in conjunction with exhaust gas assisted fuel reforming in a compression ignition engine are also investigated. The result shown that pure biodiesel has the higher yield of hydrogen (11%vol.) in the exhaust gas reforming process compared to hydrogen production in DB50 (<;2%vol.). Hydrogen production showed a strong dependence on the oxygen to carbon (O/C) ratios and reforming operating temperatures. Thus, the use of pure biodiesel fuel has shown an attractive potential to produce hydrogen over exhaust gas reforming process in compression ignition engines.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Aerodynamic Characteristics of the Eppler-197 and Modified Eppler-197 Airfoil Sections at Mach Number from 0.4 to 0.75
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to study the aerodynamic characteristics of the modified Eppler-197 airfoil sections at high-subsonic Mach number. The mean-camber line of Eppler-197 airfoil section was used as the basic mean-camber line for the two modified airfoils. The surface around the mean-camber was created by using the symmetrical airfoil profiles, NACA64012 and NACA65012. The computational fluid dynamic code, ANSYS FLUENT, was used to determine the lift, drag, pitching-moment characteristics and drag-divergence Mach number of the modified airfoils. The flow condition in this study was at Reynolds number 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> and the Mach number varies from 0.4 to 0.75. The angle of attack was varied from the -2° to 6°. The results from calculation were compared with the data of the original Eppler-197 profile. The study shows that the modified profiles have better aerodynamic characteristics at all Mach number range. The lift-to-drag ratio of the modified profiles are higher than the original profile. The drag-divergence Mach number of modified airfoils increases between 0.69 percent to 7.15 percent at lift coefficient from 0.1 to 1.1. The rate of drag rise above the drag-divergence Mach number of the modified profiles are lower than the original profile. The pitching moment does not have significantly change.

articleTitle: Effect of Diesel – Biodiesel – Ethanol Fuel Blends on Low Temperature NOX Reduction Activity over a Lean NOX Catalyst
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The lean NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</sub> catalyst in reducing Nitrogen Oxide (NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</sub>) emission is necessary for a modern compression ignition (CI) engine. However, the high operating temperature is the main problem for the catalyst. Thus, the aim of this research is to investigate the hydrocarbon selective catalytic reduction (HC-SCR) in order to reduce nitrogen oxide containing in exhaust gas of a CI engine. The research carries out by using diesel, biodiesel and ethanol at different blending ratio as the fuel. The engine speed is kept constant at 1,500 rpm and the engine loads are varied at 25, 50 and 75 % of maximum engine load. The result shows that when increase of ratio of ethanol affect the increase of HC:NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</sub>. In diesel, biodiesel and ethanol fuel blends at a ratio of 30:20:50 shows the maximum nitrogen reduction with products from HC-SCR can reduced nitrogen oxide up to 22 %. Then increase the amount of hydrogen (approximate 3,000 and 6,000 ppm) in exhaust gas to promote the HC-SCR reaction of nitrogen oxide reduction in low temperature. The effect of hydrogen addition can reduced nitrogen oxide up to 55.26 %.

articleTitle: Biofuel Synthesis from Waste Cooking Oils and Ethyl Acetate via Interesterification under CaO Catalyst from Waste Eggshells
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: A conventional biofuel production via transesterification of fatty acids and alcohols in presence of a basic or acidic catalyst produces glycerol by-product that lowers the biofuel yield. Alternatively, interesterification reaction has been gained further attention to substitute the conventional reaction due to no glycerol formation. Furthermore, the interesterification produces a value-added by-product of triacetin, a good bio-additive as anti-knocking agent and cetane number improver. The aim of this work is to investigate the interesterification of fatty acids in waste cooking oil (WCO) and ethyl acetate (ETA) under solid catalyst calcium oxide (CaO) catalyst derived from eggshells for biofuel production. The eggshell catalyst not only reduces environmental problem, but also reduces the cost of biofuel raw material. In this study, eggshell waste was grounded after cleaning up and the powder produced was calcined at 900 C for 4 hours in a furnace. The catalyst was characterized using the Fourier transform-infrared spectroscopy and the biofuel yield was determined by the gas chromatography. A certain amount of 4.0 wt% of catalyst was consumed throughout the experiment with varied parameters such as molar ratio of WCO and ETA, reaction time and temperature. The subsequent results indicate that the CaO derived from eggshell can convert the fatty acids in WCO to biofuel with high quality according to ASTM specifications.

articleTitle: Rice Roasting Machine Using Infrared Ray
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: Roasted rice is the main raw material for cooking in Thailand, especially the northeastern part. The objectives of this study were to design and construct a roasting machine using infrared rays, and to evaluate the qualities of roasted rice. The stainless steel roasting chamber was designed as a rotatable drum with a diameter of 0.6 m and a length of 1 m. An infrared burner was mounted inside the chamber. The performance of the rice roasting machine was tested at infrared burner temperature of 750 - 800 C, and drum speed of 5-7 rpm. The results showed that the optimum roasting conditions of the machine were a drum speed of 6 rpm, infrared burner temperature of 800 C and roasting time of 40 minutes. With those conditions, roasted rice would have similar quality comparing to other roasted rice in the market.

articleTitle: Impact of angular separation between adjacent users on beamforming performance
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: The standards of wireless communication systems have been developed from single-user to multi-user communications so that users can gain a higher data transmission speed, a reduction of power consumption and wider coverage. For the multi-user transmission, a base station transmits data to a number of users employing the same frequency at the same time. So far, a beamforming technology has been taken into account to upgrade the multi-user communication systems. The beamforming technology helps the systems avoid interference in the direction of main beam. In general, the interference cannot be eliminated when it comes in the region of main beam. This means that the beam width directly affects the distance between adjacent users. Furthermore, the angular separation between adjacent users affects the beamforming performance. Therefore, this paper analyzes and simulates the effect of angular separation between adjacent users. In case that desired and interference signals are both located in the main beam region, the Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio (SINR) must be very low. However, producing a narrow beam width lets users come close to one another. This can be achieved by employing a large number of antenna elements.

articleTitle: Low CO2 Concrete Made from Calcium Carbide Residue, Palm Oil Fuel Ash, Rice Husk-Bark Ash, and Recycled Aggregates
publicationTitle: 2018 Third International Conference on Engineering Science and Innovative Technology (ESIT)
abstract: In this study, the low CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> concrete was made by using several industrial wastes in both binder and aggregates. Calcium carbide residue (CCR) mixed separately with palm oil fuel ash (PA) and rice husk-bark ash (RA), and was used as a binder instead of Portland cement in the concrete mixture. Furthermore, fine and coarse recycled aggregates were fully replaced natural aggregates in order to cast concrete specimens (CCR-PA and CCR-RA concretes). Concrete properties namely compressive strength, chloride migration, and water permeability of CCR-PA and CCR-RA concretes were evaluated and compared with the conventional concrete (CON concrete). The results indicated that the compressive strengths of CCR-PA and CCR-RA concretes tended to increase with the curing age and development of compressive strength was similar to that of CON concrete. Introduction of small amount of Portland cement (OPC) as a strength accelerator resulted in effective enhancement of compressive strengths of CCR-PA and CCR-RA concretes. CCR-RA concrete contained 20% of OPC had the highest compressive strength of 34.4 and 40.9 MPa at 28 and 90 days, respectively. This compressive strength could be achieved by using 90 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of OPC. It was also found that the chloride migration and water permeability coefficient values of CCR-PA and CCR-RA concretes were similar to or lower than those of CON concrete. Moreover, the use of CCR-PA and CCR-RA binders in the concrete mixtures effectively improved the chloride migration and water permeability coefficient values of recycled aggregate concrete. These results also suggested that CCR-PA and CCR-RA concretes can be used as a new environmental friendly concrete because of these concretes can reduce as much as CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions and environmental problems.
